Since its founding in 1922, Foreign Affairs has been the leading forum for serious discussion of American foreign policy and global affairs. The magazine has featured contributions from many leading international affairs experts.

The Dangerous Idea Driving Today’s Wars of Choice

Stephen Biddle, Sam Winter-Levy, and Yuri Zhukov

Military victory is an alluring idea. A short, violent campaign that defeats the enemy promises payoffs at a tolerable price. The Trump administration expected such an outcome in Iran in February 2026. The Netanyahu government sought it in Gaza in October 2023, then in Lebanon and Iran. Russian President Vladimir Putin assumed his 2022 invasion of Ukraine would deliver it. Many critics of U.S. policy in Afghanistan and Iraq decry a failure to achieve military victory, contrasting such wars with the decisive battlefield outcomes they believe were achieved in the 1990–91 Gulf War and World War II. Trump approves military firing squad for 'jihadist' Army sergeant major who massacred 13 at Fort Hood

Actual Article Body:
By STEPHEN M. LEPORE, US SENIOR REPORTER

Published:  11:14 AEST, 6 October 2026   |  Updated:  19:12 AEST, 6 October 2026

President Trump said the former Army major turned jihadist who killed 13 people and wounded 30 in a mass shooting at Fort Hood will face death by firing squad.

Nidal Hasan claimed he launched the terror attack over anger about being deployed to Afghanistan and a desire to protect Islamic and Taliban leaders from US troops.

He was sentenced to death following the 2009 shooting.

Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell declared that Hasan will be just the second person since 2010 to be put to death by a firing squad Monday.
